newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Aug 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Nickel and cobalt producer QNI Ltd will today release further details of its merger with South Africa's Gencor base metals division, Billiton Plc. The announcement is expected to include extra incentives for QNI shareholders to agree to the merger, incluing increased capital returns and a re-evaluation for Billiton assets. Page 19.

Pearson group executive director David Bell has confirmed the company, which holds the Financial Times newspaper, is considering acquiring the Australian Financial Review but has refuted suggestions this would lead to the Financial Times becoming a "third force" in Australian media. Bell says the Financial Time's strategy would continue to focus on being a niche business publisher in global and regional markets. Page 20.

Mining giant Rio Tinto Ltd has sold 45 per cent of the prospective Wafi copper gold project in Papua New Guinea to Provincial Gold Fields for approximately A$60 million. The sale, announced yesterday, is preliminary to a full joint venture agreement whicH will be concluded at the end of next month. Page 20.

Investment company Thorney Industries has reaped massive profits from the sell-down of its stake in Austrim Ltd. Thorney yesterday announced it was no longer a major shareholder in the company, and that its sale of 1.9 million Austrim shares had garnered at least A$8.9 million. Page 20.

Hospital operator Ramsay Health is expected to agree next Monday to its float on the Australian Stock Exchange. Broker company County NatWest has begun preparing for the lodgement of a prospectus and has completed negotiations with Ramsay for underwriting fees. Page 21.

In a report to the Australian Stock Exchange, BHP Coal has forecast an increase in coking sales as world crude steel production rises. In the year ended May 31, BHP produced 54.85 million metric tons of coal, an increase of 5.7 per cent, with shipment riing to 53.84 million tons from 52.42 million tons. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

A survey of corporate leaders, prepared by The Economist Intelligence Unit, is believed to contain sharp criticism of the Australian Government's peak economic advisory agency, the Industry Commission. Those corporate leaders surveyed claim that Austraia is failing to attract international investment because the Industry Commission does not understand business. Page 21.

Power Pacific, the company owned by Queensland brewer Bernie Power, was placed in receivership last week. Power enjoyed great success in the late 1980s and early 1990s with his local beer brand which appealed to Queensland residents and captured 20 per cent of the State market. Page 21.

The farm sector is increasingly nervous about the looming drought, which is expected to be Australia's worst since 1982. Producers are already buying up stock feed on a scale unrivalled since the early 1980s, with the pressure of the expected wheat shortage pushing prices up following its recent plunge from its 30-year height last year of A$275 a tonne to A$180 tonne today. Page 21.

The Australian Securities Commission yesterday issued a practice note for lawyers and accountants containing a list of guidelines for issuing prospectuses, effective immediately. The move is a reaction against recent inaccurate profit forecasts for new share-market listings. Page 21.

The National Australia Bank is set to renew its efforts to acquire the Republic of Ireland's Trustee Savings Bank, with the newly-elected centre-right Irish Government expected to approve the sale. NAB is expected pay considerably more than its original bidding price of A$240 million. Page 23.

Telecommunications company Optus has overlooked overseas-based satellite service providers and signed a three-year agreement with the ntional Ten television network for the supply of network linking satellite services. The deal will allow the Ten Network to send programs using Optus' earth stations within Australia to Ten stations using satellite technology. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The two rival groups for the building rights to the A$300 million Docklands Stadium in Melbourne have begun lobbying institutional investors for funding. One consortium,consisting of construction company Baulderstone Hornibrook and KPMG, is seeking to raise A$104 million through a high yielding bond issue. Page 27.

Energy Developments announced yesterday it had passed regulatory obstacles and was now able to finalise a A$69 million alliance with US company NRG Energy Inc. Energy shareholders will be asked at an extraordinary meeting next month to approve the acquisition by NRG of an increased equity interest in the company to 35 per cent. Page 29.

The Macquarie/ASSIRT Retiree Price Index, released yesterday, found the cost of retirement increased in the year to June 1997 and outstripped inflation. Costs rose by 1.1 per cent, in contrast to the Consumer Price Index which showed only a 0.3 per cent ise over the same period. Page 29.

The Institute of Engineers, Australia, warned yesterday that air safety and service standards could be jeopardised if the Australian Government did not guarantee a strict regulatory framework during the second wave of airport privatisations. Page 29.

Perth-based Kilkenny Gold has launched a A$15.5 million scrip take-over bid for Kalmet Resources. Kilkenny's offer is conditional on it being able to acquire 90 per cent of Kalmet shares and all options. Page 30.

Leading Australian bloodstock company, the Arrowfield Group is planning to acquire the 10 per cent of its shares still owned by collapsed merchant bank Tricontinental for A$2.7 million. The deal will be financed by the sale of Arrowfield's Turangga Broodmare Farm in New South Wales. Page 30.
THE AGE

According to Aussie Home Loans, the Commonwealth Bank's latest advertising campaign for its no-frills Economiser home loans, which claim to provide better value than Aussie's offer, is misleading and deceptive. Page B1.

A survey of 500 business people conducted by hotel chain Hyatt Hotels and Resorts, has revealed that one in eight business travellers would be interested in a romance while working away from home. Page B1.

Mildara Blass, the wine division of Foster's Brewing Group, has spent A$160 million acquiring Cellarmaster, Australia's biggest mail-order wine-club business. The move is seen as the foundation of Mildara's overseas expansion plans. Page B1.

Stagnant retail trading conditions and a chronic stock problem are expected to force Just Jeans to reduce or scrap its final dividend following indications of an after-tax profit of A$5 million compared with the record A$14.4 million for 1995-6. Page B1.

Australian film and entertainment company Village Roadshow has offered to buy the Laguna Quays resort, in the Whitsunday region, out of bankruptcy for A$20 million from its Japanese owners Aqua del Rey International and Laguna Quays Resort. Page B1.

A press release from Federal Treasurer Peter Costello announcing Government plans to alter the tax base for depreciation of "exempt entity" assets that become depreciable for tax purposes has put into doubt the Victorian Government's privatisation programme. Page B1.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
